answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: stake-proportional sortition. Each decision seat is filled by lottery where draw probability equals an identity's share of total stake locked in a vault, not one ticket per account. Splitting a fixed stake across a thousand fakes gives the same summed probability as holding it in one, so breadth buys nothing: the lantern of selection shines on committed stake, not head count. To raise its odds a fleet must commit genuine locked value, the exact signal rewarded, so sybil multiplication sends no extra signal.
